title: Microsoft publishes Nobel economist's bearish AI forecast of just 1.5% GDP growth over a decade
key_facts: Microsoft published a piece by Nobel-winning economist Daron Acemoglu.
He predicts about 1.5% GDP boost over ten years.
He says AI will replace at most 5% of jobs.
He says companies must reassign tasks, upskill and restructure before gains arrive, maybe slower than electrification.
He says AI that extends human skills beats full automation.
He admits AI development pace is hard to predict.
It ran in Microsoft's blog 'The Humanist Review of AI'; The Decoder notes the thesis suits Microsoft.
quote_evidence: He predicts AI will boost GDP by about 1.5 percent over ten years and replace at most five percent of jobs, far less than some AI labs forecast.
He admits the pace of AI development is hard to predict.
why_it_matters_hint: A prominent economist forecasts modest AI economic gains.
notes: Short article; The Decoder's own comment about Microsoft is its opinion.
